title: Tarka Dhal
subtitle: Spiced red lentils with a fried onion and spice finish
excerpt: Red lentils cooked until completely soft and creamy, then finished with a tarka: a hot-oil tempering of onion, cumin, garlic, and chilli poured over the dhal just before serving. A staple of Indian home cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dhal is one of the most important dishes in Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi, and Sri Lankan cooking, eaten at nearly every meal in some form. The word dhal refers both to dried lentils and to the dish made from them. Tarka (or tadka or chaunk) is the technique of blooming whole and ground spices in hot fat and adding the mixture to a dish, either at the start or the end of cooking. Tarka dhal at the end, poured sizzling over the cooked lentils, is the standard finishing technique for this dish.

content.text: The lentils should cook until completely dissolved into a thick, creamy mass. If they look grainy they need more time. The tarka is the final step and should be done at the last moment: heat the oil until very hot, add the spices, watch them sizzle for 30 seconds, then pour the whole thing straight over the dhal. The sizzle as the hot oil hits the cooked lentils is part of the experience.

Put the lentils in a large pan with the water, turmeric, minced garlic, and ginger. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils have completely dissolved and the dhal is thick and creamy. Season with salt and lemon juice.

Make the tarka: heat the ghee in a small pan over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden and crispy at the edges. Add the cumin seeds, mustard seeds, chilli flakes, and sliced garlic. Cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the seeds pop and the garlic is golden.
Pour the hot tarka over the dhal. Scatter with fresh coriander. Serve immediately with basmati rice or chapati.
